questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Belize?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Belize article.

questions.proof: Belmopan, which is near the centre of the country, is its capital.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Belize?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Belize on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Belize article.

questions.proof: It shares a border on the north with the Mexican state of Quintana Roo, on the west with the Guatemalan department of Petén, and on the south with the Guatemalan department of Izabal.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Belize?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Belize article.

questions.proof: Belize is the only English-speaking country in Central America.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “This is because Belize is a former colony of the United Kingdom, while its neighbors were once colonies of _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “colonies”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Belize article.

questions.proof: This is because Belize is a former colony of the United Kingdom, while its neighbors were once colonies of Spain.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It used to be called British Honduras, but changed its name in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Belize article.

questions.proof: It used to be called British Honduras, but changed its name in 1973.
